strengths: Identifies a concrete and well-motivated failure mode (functional entanglement) in LLM-driven NAS with clear examples and intuitive explanation
Strong empirical results: 28.1× sample-efficient speedup and +15.6 pp accuracy gain on DFS, with consistent improvements across 10 CLRS tasks

Comprehensive evaluation with proper baselines, thorough ablations (Table 2) showing both ASR and RC+SAR contribute meaningfully, and insightful search dynamics analysis (Figure 2) coupling entanglement, executability, and progress
Well-designed factorization approach: the three-stage decomposition (ASR→RC→SAR) is principled, with factor-respecting feasibility formally grounded (Eq. 4)
Gains achieved without capacity scaling—MACs remain comparable to baseline, demonstrating structural improvements rather than compute expansion
Clear presentation with effective motivation figures and detailed algorithm descriptions; supplementary material provides evolution traces showing principled progression
weaknesses: Severely limited generalization scope: evaluated only on CLRS algorithmic reasoning benchmark; no discussion of how to identify/define factors for new domains, making practical applicability unclear beyond this specific benchmark

Requires significant manual engineering: factor region definition, boundary tag annotation, and task-specific feasibility checking (semantic checks require forward-pass validation specific to CLRS) create bottlenecks for new domains

Moderate technical novelty: constraining code generation to specific regions is established (Yin & Neubig 2017); the core contribution is applying this to identify entanglement in NAS, which is incremental
Incomplete handling of failure cases: substantial degradation on several tasks unexplained (BFS: 99.7%→70.6%, FW: 48.5%→32.9%, KMP: 19.5%→14.9%), raising questions about when SPARK fails

Evaluation design concerns: (1) transfer-only protocol (search on DFS, evaluate on others) reduces evidence of effectiveness; (2) EvoPrompting comparison conflates proposal efficiency with evaluation efficiency; (3) main results use single LLM (DeepSeek-R1); (4) SPARK uses OpenEvolve as both baseline and backbone, complicating attribution
Limited statistical rigor: no confidence intervals or significance tests; five seeds mentioned but not fully reported; single-iteration variant shows instability on some tasks

Insufficient analysis of discovered architectures: why are discovered patterns beneficial? How does context-conditioned gating improve algorithmic reasoning? Lacks deeper understanding of what LLM priors activate

strengths: Clear identification of 'functional entanglement' as a concrete failure mode in LLM-driven NAS with good motivation and examples
Well-designed three-step decomposition (ASR-RC-SAR) with intuitive 'where-then-how' editing primitive
Strong empirical results on CLRS with impressive speedup (28.1×) and accuracy gains (68.14%→83.74% on DFS)
Thorough ablation studies (Table 2) and search dynamics analysis (Figure 2) showing tight coupling between entanglement, validity, and progress
Solid experimental controls: single seed architecture, identical backbone/LLM across comparisons, comprehensive algorithms
Gains are not confounded by model capacity scaling (MACs remain stable at ~665K vs baseline 661K)
weaknesses: Extremely narrow evaluation scope: only CLRS algorithmic reasoning benchmark, no standard NAS benchmarks (NAS-Bench, ImageNet), severely limiting generalizability claims

Critical generalizability gap: factor factorization (OPERATOR/ACTION) appears specific to CLRS message-passing graphs; no methodology provided for determining factors in other domains (ResNets, Transformers, CNNs)
Inconsistent results across tasks (Table A.1): significant degradations on BFS (99.7%→70.6%), FW (48.5%→32.9%), and KMP (19.5%→14.9%); no analysis of when SPARK helps vs. fails

Experimental design concerns: (1) single seed architecture limits generalizability, (2) transfer protocol (evolve on DFS, transfer to others) differs from baselines, (3) cascade evaluation threshold (-100) not justified or ablated, (4) budget accounting inflates speedup claims
Missing critical ablations: feasibility checks not independently studied; hyperparameter sensitivity (k, k', R_asr) not analyzed; RC's contribution poorly understood; no failure mode analysis
Limited conceptual novelty: structured LLM prompting is straightforward; theoretical justification (p_v^k argument) is oversimplified and ignores scope feasibility correlations

Reproducibility concerns: frontier LLM dependency (DeepSeek-R1-May 2025), incomplete prompt specification, reliance on unreleased tool (OpenEvolve 2025), temperature fixed at 0.7 without justification

Incomplete theoretical understanding: connection between factor isolation and multi-round composability is claimed but not rigorously justified; why freezing ACTION during OPERATOR edits helps is not explained from first principles

strengths: Clear identification and articulation of functional entanglement as a systematic failure mode in LLM-driven NAS, with effective motivation in Figure 1
Elegant three-stage solution (ASR→RC→SAR) that directly addresses the identified problem by making functional factors explicit and enforcing single-factor edits
Strong empirical results: 28.1× sample efficiency improvement (57 vs 1600 evaluated candidates), 83.74% OOD accuracy on DFS, and 83.92% mean accuracy across 10 CLRS tasks

Rigorous experimental methodology including thorough ablations (Table 2 shows ASR alone +18.50pp, RC+SAR alone +10.01pp, combined +36.96pp), multi-seed experiments, and careful search dynamics analysis (Figure 2 ties improvements to lower entanglement, higher executability)

Controlled experimental design with fixed compute (MACs ~664K vs baseline 661K), careful budget accounting distinguishing proposals from evaluated candidates, and consistent results across multiple LLM editors
Well-designed lightweight feasibility pipeline (syntax/interface/semantic checks) and detailed program evolution analysis in appendix showing principled architectural progression
Clear presentation with effective figures, well-motivated problem setup, and comprehensive results reporting
weaknesses: Severely limited experimental scope: only evaluated on single CLRS algorithmic reasoning benchmark; no validation on CNN, RNN, Transformer, or other common NAS domains raises fundamental generalization concerns

Factorization appears hand-crafted for CLRS: OPERATOR/ACTION decomposition is specific to message-passing graph networks; no principled methodology for identifying functional factors in new domains, severely limiting applicability

Transfer protocol design raises fairness concerns: evolve on DFS then transfer to other tasks, while EvoPrompting evolves across multiple tasks simultaneously; significant performance degradation on non-evolved tasks (BFS 100%→70.6%, FW 61.4%→32.9%) suggests the transfer-only approach may hide multi-task performance limitations

Comparison fairness issues: OpenEvolve and FunSearch results obtained by running authors' code (not published comparisons); only EvoPrompting has direct published CLRS numbers, weakening independent verifiability of claimed improvements

RC (Refinement Compass) component substantially underspecified: actual mechanisms for converting search signals to directives are unclear, prompt templates not shown, and sophistication level unknown, limiting reproducibility and understanding

Insufficient statistical rigor: main results (Table 1) lack error bars or confidence intervals; multi-seed data in appendix not quantified in main text, and statistical significance of improvements not established

Missing failure case analysis: no discussion of scenarios where single-factor constraints prevent beneficial multi-factor changes, or when simultaneous OPERATOR+ACTION modifications might be necessary; Ours-1it variant unexplained

Design choice sensitivity not analyzed: MAP-Elites discretization, stagnation window k=3, proposal window k'=10 appear hand-tuned for CLRS with no ablation studies; unknown whether SPARK generalizes to other search backbones

Computational cost of LLM API calls ignored: each iteration requires 3 LLM calls; wall-clock time and monetary costs not discussed, so 'sample efficiency' gains may not translate to practical efficiency

Theoretical justification informal: feasibility degradation model (p_v^k) is intuitive but unprincipled; no formal analysis of when factor isolation is optimal or suboptimal; no characterization of problem properties favoring the approach

Limited technical novelty: structure-aware code generation and multi-stage LLM refinement are established techniques; contribution is primarily applying these to LLM-driven NAS with a domain-specific factorization, which feels incremental for a top venue

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification: Functional entanglement is clearly articulated with concrete examples; the observation about implicit coupling between Operator and Action factors is valuable for understanding LLM-driven NAS failures

Sound technical approach: Factor-isolated editing via explicit factor selection, refinement directives, and factor-conditioned patching is principled; comprehensive feasibility pipeline (syntax/interface/semantic checks) ensures generated code is executable

Thorough experimental analysis on CLRS: Strong results (83.92% on 10-task subset, 83.91% on 30-task suite); detailed ablations (Table 3, A.2) clearly demonstrate ASR and RC+SAR contributions; search dynamics tracked via entanglement rate and executability metrics

Comprehensive evaluation methodology: Fair budget accounting distinguishing proposals from evaluated candidates; multiple random seeds with uncertainty bands; clear 28.1× speedup on DFS reaching 83.74% with 57 candidates

Good presentation and reproducibility: Clear problem formulation and well-structured methodology; detailed algorithms; hyperparameters specified; code availability promised; feasibility pipeline thoroughly described
weaknesses: Limited generalization beyond CLRS: Factor-scoped approach is tightly coupled to manual OPERATOR/ACTION factorization specific to algorithmic programs; non-CLRS experiments show modest gains; no clear guidance for applying method to domains without obvious functional factors

Significant task transfer failures: Poor transfer to BFS (99.7%→70.6%), Floyd-Warshall (48.5%→32.9%), KMP (19.5%→14.9%); SPARK improves only 21/30 tasks vs CLRS reference and 19/30 vs EvoPrompting; suggests task-specific overfitting limiting practical multi-task applicability

Methodological concerns in baseline comparison: SPARK uses search-and-transfer protocol (evolve on DFS, transfer elsewhere) while EvoPrompting does multi-task evolution, making direct speedup comparison imperfect; 28.1× speedup claim is relative to 1600 evaluations under different protocol; modest ~3pp improvement on full 30-task suite (83.91% vs 80.89%) when accounting for protocol differences

Increased search-time cost not fully quantified: SPARK requires multiple LLM calls per iteration (ASR, RC, SAR) vs single-call baselines; while model-level MACs are comparable, wall-clock overhead is higher (e.g., 20news: 0.29h→0.51h in Table A.5); practical applicability when wall-clock time matters is unclear

Coarse definition of functional entanglement: Entanglement measured syntactically (cross-region line diffs); semantic entanglement could still occur within single factor; normalized diff computation (LF, whitespace) may miss functional interactions; no evidence that syntactic isolation translates to semantic isolation

Limited transfer and generalization analysis: Why do BFS, KMP, Floyd-Warshall transfer poorly? Are failures due to task-specific choices or fundamental architectural limitations? Non-CLRS experiments (Table 2) show inconsistent improvements and lack depth

Incomplete technical specifications: Prompt templates not shown; ASR retry handling could be clearer; region tag preservation via string matching is fragile; single-LLM evaluation (primary: DeepSeek-R1) limits model-agnostic claims

Alternative solutions not explored: No direct comparison with simpler approaches (e.g., prompt engineering for scoped edits); unclear if functional entanglement is necessary to address vs. achievable via better prompting or LLM selection alone

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification with clear illustration of functional entanglement and its consequences for LLM-driven NAS
Rigorous experimental design with controlled comparisons, comprehensive ablations (Table 3, A.2), and detailed search dynamics analysis (Fig. 2)
Thorough evaluation covering full 30-task CLRS suite plus 5 cross-benchmark datasets with honest discussion of limitations
Strong results on DFS task achieving 28.1× sample-efficiency improvement, with consistent improvements on multi-step compositional reasoning tasks
Clear presentation of method with algorithmic specifications and extensive supplementary material including program evolution traces
weaknesses: Severely limited generalization: Method is tightly coupled to CLRS with manually-defined OPERATOR/ACTION factors; no principled methodology provided for discovering factors in new domains; cross-benchmark results inconsistent (MNIST-1D +25.74pp vs 20News +2.03pp vs Mice Protein 0pp)

Significant and unexplained empirical failures: Catastrophic degradation on BFS (99.7→70.6), Floyd-Warshall (48.5→32.9), KMP (19.5→14.9); underperforms on 11/30 CLRS tasks; no postmortem analysis of why factor isolation fails on these tasks

Cost accounting and fairness concerns: SPARK uses 3 LLM calls per iteration vs. single-call baselines; 28.1× speedup computed only for DFS task at 57 candidates; total wall-clock time comparisons absent from main text; search-and-transfer protocol artificially concentrates budget on one task unlike multi-task baselines

Weak technical validation of core assumptions: Factor isolation assumption (Eq. 4) relies on post-hoc line-based diff and may miss semantic cross-factor changes; region tag enforcement and failure rates unreported; domain-specific engineering requirements (factor identification, feasibility checks) make generalization unclear

Limited understanding of when the method works: No analysis of what task properties determine success vs. failure; why does isolated editing help on DFS (+36.96pp) but hurt on BFS (-29.1pp)? No satisfactory explanation provided

Rigorous analysis of search dynamics (Fig. 2) directly measuring entanglement rate, validity, and showing tight coupling to progress
